plot: At the night-time Wheelburg Sleepover Turbo's three bananas vanish and he loudly blames Grumpy without checking; Bolt tests Grumpy and Pip (both honest), tiny tracks in the dew seem to lead to Bertha but turn out to be Bertha's toddler cousin Tot, who thought the bananas were yellow telephones; Turbo apologises to Grumpy (lesson: don't blame before you know), Bertha shares a snack, then something rings in the night.

script.title: 3 Bananas Vanished at the Sleepover! 🍌🌙 Who Did It?
script.description: At the Wheelburg Sleepover, Turbo's three bananas disappear in the night, and Turbo blames Grumpy before checking! Inspector Bolt puts Grumpy and Pip in the Truth Press, then follows tiny tracks in the morning dew to a very surprising little guest. Don't blame before you know. Inspector Bolt #8

set.place: Wheelburg square, sleepover night and morning

beats.say: Zoom! Honk! Beep! It's the Wheelburg Sleepover, and everyone rushed in with their pillows!
Sleepover snacks! I brought three bananas. One, two, three. Nobody touch them!
Three bananas for one car? That's a lot of banana!
Fast cars need fast snacks. One for tonight, two for breakfast.
And I brought a very special guest. My little cousin, Tot! Say hello, Tot!
Hi-hi! I'm Tot! I'm this many!
Tiny cars are noisy. I'm going to sleep now. Goodnight.
The moon rose over Wheelburg. One by one, every car closed its eyes.
Snore... honk-snore... whistle-snore. Everyone was fast asleep. Or were they?
When the sun came up, Turbo woke with a very hungry engine.
Breakfast time! Banana number one... wait. Where is banana number one?
My bananas! All three! Somebody ate my breakfast!
It was YOU, Grumpy! You always stare at my bananas!
Huh? What? I was sleeping. I'm still sleeping. Go away.
See? He didn't even say no! Grumpy is the banana thief!
Beep beep! Just then, Inspector Bolt rolled in for the sleepover breakfast.
Good morning. Turbo, I could hear you from across town. What is all this shouting?
Grumpy took my bananas! I just know it! Arrest him, Inspector!
Turbo, did you see Grumpy take them?
Well... no. I was asleep. But he looks like a banana thief!
Looking like something is not a clue. First we check. Then we know.
Thank you. I look like a tow truck. Not a banana thief.
Grumpy, would you take the Truth Press, so everyone can be sure?
Fine. Squeeze me. There's nothing in here but sleepy.
Grumpy, did you eat Turbo's bananas?
No. I don't even like bananas. I like looking at them. That's different.
Squeeze! Grumpy's eyes stayed small. He was telling the truth.
Small eyes? But... but I was so sure!
Being sure is not the same as knowing, Turbo.
Can I go next? Then everyone knows I'm honest too!
Very kind, Pip. Did you eat the bananas?
No! I only had strawberry jelly. And a tiny bit of toast.
The press gave Pip a gentle squeeze. Her eyes stayed tiny.
See? Tiny eyes! I'm honest, and I'm full of jelly!
Honest. Thank you, Pip.
Inspector Bolt looked very carefully at the ground next to Turbo's bed.
And there, in the shiny morning dew, were tiny little tyre tracks.
Tiny tracks. They go from Turbo's bed, all the way over... there.
To me? Oh my! I didn't move all night. I snore far too loudly to sneak!
That's true. Her snoring kept me awake half the night.
And these tracks are much too small for a big bus. Someone smaller made them.
Then, from behind Big Bertha, came a tiny little voice.
Ring ring! Hello? Is this the moon? Ring ring!
Little Tot rolled out, holding a banana like a telephone.
My banana! Tot, you took my bananas?
They're not bananas! They're telephones! Yellow telephones! Ring ring!
Oh, Tot. At home she has a toy phone, yellow and curvy, just like a banana.
I called the moon all night! Then I got hungry. So I ate two telephones.
She ate the telephones! That's the funniest thing I've ever heard!
Oh no. Grumpy. I said it was you, and it wasn't. I'm really sorry.
You shouted at me before you checked. That made me feel bad.
You're right. Next time I'll check first, before I blame anybody.
Okay. Apology accepted. Now please be quiet. I'm still sleepy.
Today's lesson. Don't blame before you know. Check first, then speak.
Sorry, Turbo! I didn't know they were your telephones.
That's okay, Tot. You're little. Keep that one. It's a very good telephone.
Yay! Ring ring! Hello, Turbo? You're my friend!
Hello, Tot! Yes, I'm your friend!
But Turbo's tummy-engine was still empty. Grrrumble.
Don't worry, Turbo! I always carry extra snacks for the children!
And out came a big yellow banana, just for Turbo.
Bertha, you're the best bus in the whole wide world!
Can everybody stop being happy so loudly? Some of us are sleeping.
Mystery solved. Remember, Wheelburg. Check first, then speak.
Everyone shared a big, happy sleepover breakfast together.
But that night, when everyone was fast asleep again...
Inspector Bolt, wake up! Tot is asleep, but something is still ringing!
Who is calling in the middle of the night? Find out next time in Wheelburg!
